html:
The Sinhala Only Act was a 1956 law of Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, that made Sinhala the only official language in place of English and left out Tamil.

Prime Minister S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike won power that year on a promise to lift up the Sinhalese majority, about seven in ten people, who felt shut out by an English speaking elite. For Sri Lankan Tamils, it meant losing government jobs and schooling in their own language. Tamil members of parliament who protested with a sit in were attacked, and riots followed in 1956 and 1958.

Bandaranaike tried a deal with Tamil leaders, but dropped it under pressure and was shot dead in 1959. Tamil became an official language only in 1987. By then the anger the act fed had become an armed revolt: Black July in 1983 opened the Sri Lankan Civil War, which lasted until 2009.
sum: The Sinhala Only Act was a 1956 law of Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, that made Sinhala the only official language in place of English and left out Tamil.
